similar_scenes.name: Speed/thrash metal
similar_scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
similar_scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
similar_scenes.desc: Si el lite metal es la corriente latitudinaria, el speed/thrash es la fundamentalista: un retorno a los principios de la subcultura heavy que, como todo fundamentalismo, es tanto un comienzo nuevo como una continuación. Nace en California en 1981-83 con Metallica en Los Ángeles y Exodus en San Francisco; hacia 1982 hay una escena de fans que intercambian maquetas y grabaciones piratas, y durante años solo graba en sellos independientes y suena en programas de radio universitaria: «underground» también en lo comercial. Bebe de la NWOBHM (Venom, Diamond Head, Iron Maiden) y del punk y el hardcore. Weinstein lo compara con la Reforma protestante: fuera la ropa de escena, el atrezo y la distancia; los músicos visten vaqueros y camiseta, se mezclan con el público y se tiran a él desde el escenario. Acelera el tempo, renuncia a lo dionisíaco (el alcohol y las drogas son malos, no hay sexo) y se especializa en un caos concreto: alienación, corrupción política, destrucción ambiental, una retórica de canción protesta.

similar_scenes.name: Speed y thrash metal
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: La escena «street» de Los Ángeles cruza el hardcore (Bad Brains, Black Flag) con el glam-metal. A partir de una intuición de D.R.I., Metallica inventan el speed-metal: del thrash de Kill 'Em All a la elegancia casi clásica de Master Of Puppets. Megadeth, Slayer (puente entre el black metal de Venom y el death metal), Exciter, la escena de San Francisco (Death Angel, Exodus, Testament), Anthrax y White Zombie en Nueva York, y Sepultura, que lo convierten en lenguaje universal (Roots).

podcast.title: 2010s Performance and Revival
podcast.body: Thrash Metal performed "okay" in the 2010s, though not reaching the heights of its 80s and 90s popularity. Metallica led the way with the album "Hardwired...to Self-Destruct" and a highly profitable tour. The other "Big Four" bands—Slayer, Megadeth, and Anthrax—also released top 10 albums. A Thrash Metal revival was noted with newer bands like Municipal Waste, Power Trip, and Warbringer, though none approached the success of the Big Four. "Thrash Metal did okay, although not as well as what we saw in the 80s and the 90s." "And we can say that we saw a Thrash Metal revival with bands like Municipal Waste, Power Trip and Warbringer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Anthrax as Kings
podcast.body: Anthrax is specifically referred to as one of the "Thrash Metal King's," indicating their prominence in the genre. "he joined Thrash Metal King's Anthrax in 1983 as a lead guitarist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emergence from Hardcore Influence
podcast.body: Thrash metal developed as a direct result of hardcore punk's influence on metal music. Metal bands started adopting the faster tempos and harder-hitting aggression characteristic of hardcore, creating a new, more intense subgenre. "Hardcore punk began to influence metal. Metal bands started playing faster and harder, resulting in thrash metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Massive Commercial Phenomenon in the 80s
podcast.body: In the 1980s, Thrash Metal became a massive commercial phenomenon. Despite its extreme sound, characterized by double bass drumming and distinctive solos from bands like Metallica, Megadeth, and Slayer, it achieved great success, contributing significantly to metal's widespread popularity. "Durante esa década, el metal ya se había convertido en un fenómeno masivo. El Trash Metal con su doble bombo y sus solos características de bandas como Metallica, Mega Death, Wes Lager, gozaba de gran éxito comercial, pesa tener un sonido tan extremo."

srcs.episode: El DOOM METAL es el DARK SOULS de la música

podcast.title: Neurosis's Pursuit of Heaviness
podcast.body: Neurosis, recognized as legends of Thrash Metal and Post Metal, sought Steve Albini to produce their album *Times of Grace* with the explicit goal of achieving an even heavier and drier sound than their previous works. This decision reflects the genre's continuous push for sonic intensity. "la leyenda del Slash Metal y Post Metal Neurosys tras la obra maestra que fue el anterior disco Throxil Verimblod de 1996, pensaron que aún podrían sonar más pesados y secos, por lo que contactaron Albindli para grabar su nuevo disco, Timesoft Free Grace, y vayas si lo consiguió."

srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Offshoot of Hardcore Punk
podcast.body: Thrash Metal emerged as a direct consequence of hardcore punk. Some of the musical innovations and intensity from hardcore acts directly influenced metal musicians, leading to the birth of this new subgenre. "and some of what they did landed in the laps of some of the metal kits, resulting in the birth of Thrash Metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest
